external_entities.name: user's browser
external_entities.description: A user's browser outside the system's network.
external_entities.source_excerpt: A user's browser talks to the web application

processes.name: web application
processes.description: The web application receives browser traffic, enqueues jobs, and reads its configuration.
processes.source_excerpt: The web application does not do the heavy work itself. It puts jobs onto a message queue

processes.name: background worker
processes.description: A background worker process that picks up jobs, performs the work, and reads and writes the database.
processes.source_excerpt: a background worker process picks them up and does the work

data_stores.name: message queue
data_stores.description: A queue containing jobs placed by the web application and picked up by the background worker.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It puts jobs onto a message queue

data_stores.name: database
data_stores.description: The database read and written by the background worker and used to keep application log records.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The background worker reads and writes the database. The database is also where we keep the application's log records.

data_stores.name: web application config
data_stores.description: Configuration read by the web application, including the credentials it needs for the queue.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the web application has a web application config

data_stores.name: worker config
data_stores.description: Configuration read by the worker, including the credentials it needs for the database.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the worker has a worker config

data_flows.name: browser traffic
data_flows.description: The user's browser communicates with the web application.
data_flows.source_excerpt: A user's browser talks to the web application over HTTP/S across the public internet.

data_flows.name: enqueue jobs
data_flows.description: The web application puts jobs onto the message queue.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It puts jobs onto a message queue

data_flows.name: pick up jobs
data_flows.description: The background worker picks jobs up from the message queue.
data_flows.source_excerpt: a background worker process picks them up

data_flows.name: read and write database
data_flows.description: The background worker reads and writes the database, including application log records.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The background worker reads and writes the database.

data_flows.name: read configuration
data_flows.description: The web application reads its settings and queue credentials from its configuration store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Both processes read their settings from a config store: the web application has a web application config

data_flows.name: read configuration
data_flows.description: The background worker reads its settings and database credentials from its configuration store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: the worker has a worker config

trust_boundaries.name: outside our network
trust_boundaries.description: The network area where the user's browser sits, outside the system's network.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The browser sits outside our network

trust_boundaries.name: web tier
trust_boundaries.description: The tier where the web application runs.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: the web application runs in our web tier

trust_boundaries.name: backend tier
trust_boundaries.description: The tier containing the queue, worker, and database, behind the web tier.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The queue, the worker and the database are all in the backend tier, behind the web tier.

assumptions.assumption: The web application is internet-facing because a user's browser reaches it across the public internet.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the browser talks to the web application across the public internet.

assumptions.assumption: The background worker presents a non-web interface because it is described as a background worker process rather than a web-facing application.
assumptions.basis: The source describes a background worker process that picks up jobs and does work.

assumptions.assumption: The web application configuration is confidential because it holds queue credentials.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the web application config holds the web application's queue credentials.

assumptions.assumption: The worker configuration is confidential because it holds database credentials.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the worker config holds the worker's database credentials.
